findings.observation: The sheet index on Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) does not list a dedicated 'Addressing Plan' sheet. However, addressing information is present on the overall site plan sheets. Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) shows building labels, driveway access points, parking garage, handicap parking symbols, and sidewalk/ADA path designations. Sheet 15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 2 of 2) includes Key Note 7 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE' with hexagon symbols marking entrance locations, and a LEGEND defining building entrance symbols, ADA paths, ADA ramps, and handicap parking symbols.
findings.reasoning: The deficiency states 'Addressing information not shown on an Addressing Plan sheet or the overall site plan sheet, or not listed in Sheet Index'. While no dedicated Addressing Plan sheet exists, the addressing information IS shown on the overall site plan sheets (13, 14, 15). The requirement is satisfied by the first condition (shown on overall site plan sheet), making the sheet index listing optional. This is consistent with CC Submittal Checklist p.2 guidance that addressing may be shown 'on an Addressing Plan sheet or the overall site plan sheet'.
findings.explanation: Addressing information is shown on overall site plan sheets 13, 14, and 15, including building entrances, driveways, parking, and pedestrian access.

findings.observation: Sheet 15 includes Key Note 7 explicitly labeled 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE' in the KEY NOTES table. Hexagon symbol '7' appears in at least two locations along the eastern facade of Proposed Building 1 facing South Lamar Boulevard. The LEGEND also includes a dashed semi-circle symbol corresponding to 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE'.
findings.reasoning: Main building entrances are labeled using the standard key note system, which is an accepted method for identifying site features on civil plans. The entrances are clearly marked with symbols, defined in both the key notes table and legend, and positioned on the plan view. This satisfies the requirement for labeling main front entrance, building doors, entries, and access points.
findings.explanation: Building entrances are labeled via Key Note 7 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE' on Sheet 15, with symbols marking entrance locations on the plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 13 shows two driveway access points along Collier Street labeled 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS'. Handicap parking spaces are indicated with painted wheelchair symbols in the surface parking area on the eastern side near Collier St and South Lamar Blvd; Sheet 15 LEGEND defines 'PROPOSED HANDICAP PARKING' symbol. Sheet 13 labels the garage as 'PARKING GARAGE SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DETAILS'. Sidewalk access is indicated via 'PROPOSED ADA PATH' (shown in legends on both sheets with dotted line symbols), '5' SIDEWALK' and '8' SIDEWALK' labels, and 'VARIABLE WIDTH PUBLIC SIDEWALK EASEMENT' along Collier Street. Sheet 15 Key Note 12 identifies 'PROPOSED ADA RAMP' locations.
findings.reasoning: All four elements required by this item are identified on the plans: (1) driveway access points are explicitly labeled, (2) handicap parking is shown with wheelchair symbols and defined in the legend, (3) garage area is explicitly labeled, and (4) sidewalk access is indicated through ADA path symbols, sidewalk labels, and ADA ramp callouts. The requirement asks for identification, which can be satisfied through labels, symbols, or legend entries - all of which are present here.
findings.explanation: Driveway access points, handicap parking, parking garage, and sidewalk/ADA access are all identified on Sheets 13 and 15.

findings.observation: The official project name displayed in the prominent title/header area of Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) is '1700 SOUTH LAMAR', which is the literal street address. This same name appears in title blocks throughout the plan set.
findings.reasoning: The deficiency explicitly describes project names that include address numbers (e.g., '1515 Main St Commons' instead of 'Main St Commons'). The project name '1700 SOUTH LAMAR' begins with the street address number '1700', violating the guidance from CC Submittal Checklist p.2 and 911 Addressing Standards that project names should be descriptive (not address-based) to avoid confusion in emergency response systems.
findings.explanation: Project name '1700 SOUTH LAMAR' includes the street address number, violating addressing standards.
findings.resolution: Change project name to remove the address number. Use a descriptive name (e.g., 'South Lamar Commons' or 'Lamar Mixed-Use') instead of '1700 South Lamar'.
